feedback.problem: A data set contains the observations ${x}_{1}=28,{x}_{2}=18$ with $z$-scores ${z}_{1}=3.6$ and ${z}_{2}=1.1,$ respectively. Find the mean of the data set.
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overset{―}{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma ,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma 
$$

From the first observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}28 & =\overset{¯}{x}+3.6\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

From the second observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}18 & =\overset{¯}{x}+1.1\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

Subtracting the second equation from the first and solving for $\sigma ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(28-18) & =(3.6-1.1)\cdot \sigma  \\ 10 & =2.5\cdot \sigma  \\ \sigma  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this value back into our first equation and solving for $\overset{¯}{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}28 & =\overset{¯}{x}+3.6\cdot \sigma  \\ 28 & =\overset{¯}{x}+3.6\cdot 4 \\ \overset{¯}{x} & =13.6.\end{aligned}
$$
